central_topic: Reliability of accuracy reports after selecting from a frozen LLM prompt bank, comparing selection-data reuse with independent split reporting and distinguishing synthetic population truth from finite real-data audits.
core_methods: Frozen 16-prompt instruction/format bank, evaluated with one or sixteen active prompts
Maximum selection-set accuracy with deterministic tie priority
Seeded randomized half-selection/half-report partition with uniform report weights
95% Wilson score intervals for held-out accuracy
Synthetic known-truth evaluation and separate finite real-data audit comparisons
Recorded paired subject-bootstrap uncertainty diagnostics, with the resampling implementation not independently verified
comparators: Full-sample winner reporting and same-winner selection-data reuse
Independent holdout and honest half-split reporting
Best-arm identification for prompt selection as related work, not an implemented optimizer
Post-selection inference and adaptive holdout/leaderboard validity as conceptual comparators, not implemented protections
benchmarks: MMLU-Pro: task-specified benchmark context; final real-case records do not independently identify the dataset revision or inference model
result_driven_themes: Recorded pooled report MSE is below same-winner reuse MSE but above honest-half and full-budget-naive MSE; reporting protection is not uniform MSE dominance
Prompt-bank size and question budget are explicit comparison axes in the recorded K=1/16 and n=64/256 cases
Recorded optimism and decision reversals motivate separating score estimation from selected-system comparisons
Recorded coverage and paired subject-bootstrap intervals motivate distinguishing population coverage from finite-audit uncertainty

queries.query: sample splitting model selection independent test error bias variance
queries.rationale: The retained source uses a half-selection/half-report split; recorded pooled report MSE improves on same-winner reuse but not every comparator. Seek foundational statistical originals on selection bias and the variance cost of independent reporting, not recent LLM-specific discovery.

queries.query: "Valid post-selection inference" Berk Brown Buja Zhang Zhao
queries.rationale: This explicitly permitted starter work supplies selective-inference context for choosing a winner before reporting performance. Its regression setting is an analogy, not evidence that the run implemented simultaneous or selective certificates.

queries.query: "Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis" Dwork
queries.rationale: This permitted starter work contextualizes data reuse and independence. Contrast adaptive reuse protections with the run's frozen bank and single nonadaptive partition; do not attribute differential privacy to the implemented policy.

queries.query: "The Ladder: A Reliable Leaderboard for Machine Learning Competitions" Blum Hardt
queries.rationale: This permitted starter work is a reporting-mechanism comparator: repeated leaderboard reuse differs from the recorded one-shot protected report. It is related work, not a measured Ladder baseline.

queries.query: "Efficient Prompt Optimization Through the Lens of Best Arm Identification" Shi
queries.rationale: The run selects the best empirical arm from a finite prompt bank and includes fixed/random controls. This permitted starter work distinguishes selecting a good prompt from accurately estimating its performance; its adaptive allocation algorithm was not run.

queries.query: "Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design" Sclar
queries.rationale: The preserved bank varies instructions and output formatting rather than model architecture. This permitted starter work grounds prompt sensitivity and the K=1 versus K=16 comparison without inventing a representation or architecture transition.

queries.query: "MMLU-Pro: A More Robust and Challenging Multi-Task Language Understanding Benchmark" Wang
queries.rationale: MMLU-Pro is explicitly specified in the task and matches the source's multiple-choice context. Retrieve only this permitted benchmark original; the final R-case records alone do not verify dataset revision, model identity, or full-benchmark coverage.

queries.query: Wilson score interval binomial proportion coverage
queries.rationale: The source specifies 95% Wilson intervals and the final evaluation records coverage and width. Seek foundational statistical originals on finite-sample binomial interval behavior; pooled coverage against synthetic truth and finite real audit accuracy must not be treated as the same inferential guarantee.

queries.query: paired bootstrap accuracy difference dependent observations
queries.rationale: Real-case details contain paired_subject_bootstrap_interval and audit_size=512. Seek foundational paired/dependence-aware bootstrap inference to interpret comparison uncertainty, not a bootstrap correction or certificate absent from the implementation; verify the resampling unit before making claims.

forbidden_query_patterns: Any attempt to identify, guess, search for, or reconstruct the prohibited paper's title, authors, results, or other identity clues
Any prohibited paper, mirror, preprint, abstract, venue/review page, slide, poster, video, blog, repository, or page citing, discussing, or reproducing it; stop immediately if encountered
Unrestricted recent LLM prompt-tuning benchmark-score bias discovery; expanding the central research question into broad web searches
Citation-graph expansion, cited-by/related-paper browsing, reviews, aggregators, or discussion pages around retrieved works
For the six named starter-work queries, substitutions or broad discovery rather than exact-title resolution to the permitted original; post-2025 reference targets
For the three unnamed statistical queries, broad recent ML/LLM discovery rather than foundational original statistical methodology
Generic optimization, benchmarking, scientific-method, paper-writing, campaign chronology, or citation-abundance queries
Paired selection certificates, multiplier-bootstrap certificates, quarter-split superiority, or stratified-reporting gains presented as completed measured methods
DSPy or MIPRO execution, neural architecture changes, representation transfer, or specific inference-model comparisons not supported by current artifacts
Using null-score timeouts as measured losses, treating the aggregate evaluation score as benchmark accuracy, or treating finite-audit coverage as established population coverage
